author: Dana Whitlock
bio: Co-founder & CEO @lumenagents. AI agents that write your code. Prev eng at Halcyon.
text: Software engineering as a job is over within two years. Learn to manage agents or get left behind. The people still writing code by hand in 2028 will be hobbyists.

author: Marcus Oyelaran
bio: Member of technical staff. Training frontier models. Opinions mine.
label: Northwind AI
text: People really don't understand how good the new models are. I watched one solve in forty minutes what took our team a quarter. This is the most important technology of our lifetimes and it's not close.

author: Helena Brisk
bio: General Partner at Tidewater Ventures. Investing in AI-native companies from seed to Series B.
text: Calling it now: AGI by 2028, and every SaaS company that hasn't rebuilt around AI agents by then will be worth zero. The window to get in is closing fast.

author: Pieter Galloway
bio: I teach 40,000+ people to make money with AI. Join The Prompt Academy 👇
text: If you're not using AI every single day you are already behind. In 12 months the gap between people who learned ChatGPT and people who didn't will be impossible to close. Start today.

author: Yusuf Brandt
bio: Applied research @quillpointai, where we build LLMs for search. Previously PhD in NLP.
text: The AI doomers have been wrong at every single step. Hallucinations are basically solved, the energy numbers are made up, and 'it's just autocomplete' people should try actually using an LLM for once.

author: Ingrid Solberg
bio: Founder, Brightloop (AI copilots for lawyers). Mum of two. Oslo.
text: The EU AI Act is going to kill European AI startups before they start. Regulating models instead of uses is a gift to the incumbents. We need a moratorium on this law, not on the technology.

author: Niall Farrow
bio: Dad. Cyclist. Opinions my own.
text: We just shipped coding agents to every customer of my startup, and I'm telling you: AI replaces junior developers within a year. Half our customers have already stopped hiring them.

author: Odette Marsh
bio: Chief Cloud Economist and co-founder at Mallard Group. Author, Artificial Confidence. Professional skeptic with receipts.
note: Founded a company, has an .ai link and a book with 'Artificial' in the title, but nothing says the company's business is AI.
text: Every AI company is lighting money on fire and the cloud bills prove it. I have seen the invoices. This bubble pops within a year.

author: Colm Beaumont
bio: Professor of computer science, University of Galway. Machine learning, statistics, hill walking.
text: The benchmark numbers in most LLM papers this year don't survive contact with a held-out test set. AI progress is real but much slower than the press releases suggest, and we should say so.

author: Esme Lindahl
bio: ICU nurse. Dog person. Views my own.
text: Honestly think the new software is going to make hospital paperwork worse, not better. Every new tool they give us adds three more screens to click through before I can see a patient.

author: Frederik Mwangi
bio: Backend engineer at a logistics company. Postgres, Go, bikes.
text: Unpopular opinion: AI coding assistants are great for boilerplate and terrible for anything that needs you to understand the system. Claude saved me an hour today and cost me two yesterday.

author: Wren Hollis
bio: Developer relations @quillpointai.
text: Quillpoint 3.2 is out today. New in this release: streaming tool calls, a 200k context window on the small model, and batch pricing. Changelog and migration notes in the docs.

author: Sam Reyes
bio: Research engineer at Northwind AI. Interpretability.
text: New paper from our team: we trace how a language model does two-digit addition and find separate circuits for the carry and the ones digit. Method, code and all the negative results are in the thread.

text: Took the kids to the coast this weekend and didn't open my laptop once. Highly recommend, would do again, ten out of ten, the chips were excellent.
